newsitem.title: USA: Angeion sees slow near-term sales growth.
newsitem.headline: Angeion sees slow near-term sales growth.

text.p: Angeion Corp said Thursday that near-term sales are expected to grow at a slower rate than originally planned until its sales organization and distribution relationships are fully established.

The company said it is developing its own sales force and establishing other distribution relationships, as well as working through a dissolution of its former distribution relationship with St. Jude Medical Inc.

"While building sales of our Sentinel products is an important focus for us, we are also making great strides toward completing our U.S. clinical studies, preparing for the first human implant of our next ICD (implantable defibrillator) product, the Auracle 2020 system, and initiating U.S. clinical studies of our radio frequency catheter ablation system," said Chief Executive Whitney McFarlin.

Angeion reported sales of $766,406 for its Sentinel series of implantable cardioverter defibrillator systems for the second quarter ended January 31. This represents a 187 percent increase from a year earlier.
Sales of Angeion's Sentinel ICD systems for the second quarter rose to $708,806 from $57,600 a year earlier.
These sales were derived entirely from Angeion sales in Europe and clinical reimbursement in the U.S.
During the second quarter, no original-equipment manufacturer sales were reported from St. Jude, Angeion's former OEM distributor, Angeion said.
In addition, the company said, certain OEM revenues were not recorded during the quarter pending the outcome of negotiations to dissolve Angeion's relationship with St. Jude.
An ICD is a small electronic device implanted in the body and wired to the heart that keeps the heart from beating too fast.
